note.question: How does the bias-aware algorithm assigns less (more) weight to the clinical-risk information (radiologist’s mammogram assessment) when the mean error increase (decreases), but the reverse happens when the error variance increases?
note.overview: When algorithms use data generated by human beings, they inherit the errors stemming from human biases, which likely diminishes their performance. The paper examines the design and value of a bias-aware linear classification algorithm that accounts for bias in input data, using breast cancer diagnosis as our specific setting. In this context, a referring physician makes a follow-up recommendation to a patient based on two inputs: the patient’s clinical-risk information and the radiologist’s mammogram assessment.
